title: LIV's latest court filings paint clearest picture of league's lavish spending
article_text:
Bankruptcy filings are notoriously cumbersome, but every bankruptcy judge would admit the tedious paperwork is necessary. If a company is declaring bankruptcy, and thereby seeking some sort of legal protection against its current state, it had better be able to explain why.

But the process of doing so is a nightmare for lawyers as much as it is for their printers. It doesn’t take long for the number of pages to cross the threshold of tens of thousands. On Thursday evening alone, thousands of pages were filed in LIV Golf’s bankruptcy case, across its lot of international entities, its 13 franchises and dozens of other subsidiaries. Staring at it might send you into a daze, but there’s plenty that can be gleaned from these documents, which were prepared by LIV’s management and advisors. Thursday’s trove offered one main theme: LIV Golf owed many companies money.

Of course that’s probably implied by all we’ve known from the Saudi-backed company. But a closer look shows just how expensive it is to run any golf league, but in particular one that wanted to stunt on its competition with flashy tech and deep pockets.

Thursday’s filings included a massive list of assets and liabilities for LIV Golf Incorporated, with amounts ranging from $13.46 owed to FedEx up into the millions owed to Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau. Many of the contracts that LIV Golf maintained into September have been rejected or are expected to be rejected, but that’s beside the point. The documents are a reminder that many companies had struck a deal with LIV Golf.

Take the $178,087.50 that LIV owed to the American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers, presumably for licensing music to play at its events and on its platforms. In that case, it costs a lot of money to be Golf But Louder.

There’s the $9,350 that LIV owed to ASAP Sports, the transcription service for interviews and transcripts used across the golf industry. LIV owed $28,689.24 to AT&T and $49,609.59 to Avalara Inc., a tax and compliance company (and that’s just a few of the companies that start with the letter “A”).

There are companies for printing, insurance, travel management, public relations. There are plenty of well-known brands, like Equinox gyms, which LIV owed $22,850, or Uber, which LIV owed $89,407. And then there are several generic-sounding others, like Exciting Events Inc. (owed $7,000), Narrative Strategies LLC (owed $27,000) or SportsMEDIA Technology Corp (owed $352,418.50, a number LIV has disputed).

There are recognizable names, like broadcaster Jerry Foltz, or the Club at Chatham Hills, the host course of LIV’s final event in Indiana. But then there are others that sound a bit goofy on the surface. According to the filing, LIV owed $25,804.26 to Run Like a Deer, Inc. — the company owned by comedian Andrew Santino, who created broadcast content with LIV Golf over the years — though LIV marked it as a disputed claim.

Over the course of doing business, the league was constantly racking up one helluva tab. A lot of that became public via lawsuits it was pulled into over the summer, once the Saudi PIF made clear it was no longer funding LIV into the future — forcing LIV CEO Scott O’Neil to face questions about bankruptcy weeks before he was ready to publicly commit to it.

But beyond what was owed, there is further proof of what was paid. Like the quarterly payments of $4.946 million to Rahm — totaling just short of $20 million annually, for his Player Participation Agreement (read: contract). There was a massive settlement paid to Greg Norman in September 2025, for $5.8 million. On the same day, another $3.6 million bonus was paid to Norman, roughly eight months after he was replaced as CEO. Not far from Norman’s name on the sheet are Eugene Davis and Jon Zinman, whom LIV brought in as independent directors in April to oversee restructuring of the business, each earning $150,000 a month. (That’s right, the people brought in to settle the structure of the business and determine how new money will flow throughout it, they make a pretty penny, too.)

There’s another word that is used throughout the most recent filings: Undetermined. In the 292-page document outlining LIV Golf Incorporated’s assets and liabilities, that U-word is found 808 times. Sometimes to explain the definition of how things are noted in the filing, but otherwise to explain that the number owed to, say, Phil Mickelson, is undetermined. The amount of money LIV Golf may owe the parties who had been suing it, like World Golf Group and Premier Golf Group — who claim LIV took concepts from its original ideas — is undetermined.

All of which should just serve as one final memento of LIV Golf 1.0. It wanted to be everything, and it was paying for everything. And in the end, that didn’t work out.

title: Wales great Taulupe Faletau stood down with immediate effect
article_text:
Wales star Taulupe Faletau has suffered another cruel injury blow, just days after making his long-awaited return for Cardiff.

The 35-year-old number eight made his first appearance since March in Cardiff's Champions Cup defeat to Northampton Saints on 18 October.

He looked sharp on his return. Sadly, the comeback did not last long.

As reported by BBC Sport, Faletau complained of pain in his little finger in the days after the match.

He now needs surgery and faces another spell on the sidelines.

The veteran forward will miss Cardiff's United Rugby Championship clash with Ospreys on 31 October.

However, there is hope he could return after the November break.

Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl confirmed the setback.

"Unfortunately he had a little bit of a niggle with a pinkie finger, so he will be on the sidelines for a while," he said.

"He will miss the Ospreys game but hopefully after November he will be fine."

The news comes as another blow for Cardiff, who have had little luck keeping their star forward fit.

Last season was particularly tough. Shoulder, calf and knee injuries limited him to only seven matches.

His latest setback is all the more frustrating because he came through the Northampton match without noticing anything wrong.

"I can imagine he is quite frustrated because after the game he didn't even realise it, then the next day it was sore all of a sudden," Van Zyl explained.

"It's a tough one for him to take, but hopefully he can turn it around."

For a player who has spent so much time in the treatment room, it is another rotten slice of luck.

The timing is especially cruel for Faletau, who had been handed fresh hope of a Wales recall.

Head coach Steve Tandy left the 109-cap veteran out of his initial Nations Championship squad but insisted his international career was far from over.

"He is a legend of our game and a world-class player, so we would definitely not rule anyone out," Tandy said.

The Wales boss also backed Faletau to push for a fourth Rugby World Cup in 2027.

However, he wanted the number eight to prove he could stay fit and play regular rugby.

"I've spoken to Toby about being fit and available; then we can cross that bridge when he has put some consistent rugby together."

Tandy also made it clear that Faletau still had the hunger to play at the highest level.

"Toby is competitive. He loves playing for Cardiff and loves playing for Wales, so I can see the drive in him," he said.

This latest setback makes that task even harder.

At 35, Faletau still has plenty to offer. The problem, once again, is getting him onto the pitch.

title: Statement: All Blacks trio stood down with immediate effect
article_text:
The All Blacks have suffered a major injury blow ahead of the Nations Championship, with three forwards ruled out of the Northern Series.

Tyrel Lomax, Shannon Frizell and Samisoni Taukei'aho will all miss the trip north.

It leaves New Zealand short of options up front, just days before their squad is named on Tuesday, 27 October.

The powerful prop continues to struggle with a neck disc injury dating back to the Super Rugby season.

Lomax will remain in New Zealand for treatment and recovery. No return date has been confirmed.

Frizell suffered a PCL rupture in his left knee during the Sydney Test.

The back-row forward faces around six weeks on the sidelines, ruling him out of the Northern Series.

The hooker also picked up an injury during the Sydney Test.

Taukei'aho suffered a calf tear and faces between four and six weeks out.

His absence is another blow to New Zealand's forward depth.

- Leroy Carter – High ankle injury, underwent surgery.

- Shannon Frizell – Left knee PCL rupture.

title: Genesis Championship: Yuto Katsuragawa takes two-shot lead into final day as he ties course record with flawless 63
article_text:
Yuto Katsuragawa will take a two-stroke lead into the final day of the Genesis Championship after the Japanese golfer tied the course record on Saturday.

Katsuragawa shot a flawless eight-under 63 in the third round at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club, including four birdies in his first five holes, to match Jinam Kang's record in 2006.

The 28-year-old is 13 under overall, two shots ahead of South Africa's Casey Jarvis.

Jarvis is seeking a third win of the 2026 season, after the Kenya Open and South African Open in February, to close in on the top three in the Race to Dubai standings - Eugenio Chacarra, Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy.

Reed and McIlroy are not competing this week. Chacarra, who is No 1 in the standings after winning in India last week, was 10 shots back after the third round and tied for 30th.

There are two more events left in the European tour season, in Abu Dhabi and then Dubai.

title: DP World Tour Pros Share Thoughts On LIV Golfers Potentially Returning To Circuit
article_text:
The exodus of players from the LIV Golf League continued on Friday, as Ian Poulter, Lucas Herbert and Tyrrell Hatton were among a number of individuals to reveal that they won't be returning for LIV Golf 2.0.

Instead of plying their trade on LIV, multiple pros have expressed their desires to either return to the DP World Tour or, in some cases, plot their way onto the circuit.

It's the latter point that has caused a reaction from those on the DP World Tour, with some taking to social media to post their thoughts.

Ewen Ferguson, who has been a member of the circuit since 2022, earning three victories in that time, was one of the players to post their opinion, with it being praised by some of his fellow peers.

Writing on X, the Scotsman stated: "I have to say, some of the LIV players coming back to play DP is actually cool as some (are) really good players, but hilarious how some of them slammed the tour for so long, not one good thing to say about it, now it’s the best thing since sliced bread and feels like coming home."

Richard Mansell was in agreement with his fellow DP World Tour pro, as the Englishman himself responded to Ferguson's post.

Writing on the social media platform, Mansell said: "Spot on my mate. I haven’t been around the tour a lot this year and when I have since coming back from injury my golf hasn’t been where I want it so I don’t want to say too much.

Subscribe to the Golf Monthly newsletter to stay up to date with all the latest tour news, equipment news, reviews, head-to-heads and buyer’s guides from our team of experienced experts.

"However, things are going to look different in 2027. Some should be allowed back and some shouldn’t…"

The comments surround the idea of whether some LIV players should receive DP World Tour starts, or whether they should have to go through the circuit's Q School to earn their place on the Tour.

Jose Luis Ballester, Luis Masaveu and Michael La Sasso are among multiple LIV players listed in the Second Stage of DP World Tour Q School, while the likes of Hatton kept their DP World Tour membership, thus meaning he can make starts going forward.

Eddie Pepperell, who has been a critic of the LIV Golf League in the past, is one those who believes that there should be some thought into who earns invites into tournaments, especially when it comes to who will add viewership to the events and the possibility that DP World Tour players might miss out on playing opportunities due to LIV Golfers involvement.

Writing in his Chipping Forecast blog, the Englishman gave a balanced perspective on the matter, before stating: "My view was pretty simple, give a few players invites who undeniably add stardust.

"The Joaquin Niemann's of the world, Cam Smith, Bryson of course. Jon Rahm and Tyrell Hatton have their exemptions. Truthfully from my perspective not much else needed to be done, just ensure everybody else goes back to the qualifying school.

"The idea that Charles Howell III is on this list, with all due respect to Charles - he’s a terrific guy - is utterly bizarre.

"That represents a miscalculation to me, along frankly with additional names like Thomas Pieters, Branden Grace and even Louis Oosthuizen, as much as I admire his swing.

"None of these players are going to put enough bums on seats or in front of TVs to materially improve the balance sheet in 2027, period. I hate to sound certain about it, but I just can’t see how it can be."

The view of players having to go through Q School is a thought also shared by Lee Westwood, who settled his fines with the DP World Tour earlier this year.

"It’s an interesting position the @DPWorldTour finds itself in," he wrote on X.

"Caught between needing “names” at those times of year when they don’t get strong fields (Jan-June) Giving invites to people who have shown no interest in the Tour other than now when they’ve nowhere else to play and keeping the members happy that support the tour at the smaller events and the lads that have gone through all the qualifying stages.

"Anyone with an exemption should be free to come back because as we know the DPWT endorses members going to another rival tour and already have 10 cards for it but if people don’t have an exemption they should have to go through the school like everyone else.

"Anyone that thinks the PGA tour aren’t rivals and are partners are either blind or fools. Yes they provide funding now but to what end and at what cost to the DPWT? The end of 2027 will be interesting as to what assets they ask for."

Matt joined Golf Monthly in February 2021 covering weekend news, before also transitioning to equipment and testing. After freelancing for Golf Monthly and The PGA for 18 months, he was offered a full-time position at the company in October 2022 and continues to cover news and social media.

Taking up the game when he was just seven years of age, Matt made it into his county squad just a year later and continues to play the game at a high standard, with a handicap of around 2-4. To date, his best round is a six-under-par 66 having been seven-under through nine.

title: Two more Ryder Cup stars quit LIV Golf
article_text:
Ian Poulter is the latest LIV Golf team captain team captain to reveal he is leaving the stricken league.

The Englishman, who co-captains Majesticks GC with compatriot Lee Westwood, follows hot on the heels of Louis Oosthuizen and Jon Rahm through the LIV exit door.

In a statement on social media titled “life update”, Poulter wrote: “Hi all – I wanted everyone to hear it direct from me that I have decided to not move forward with being part of LIV 2.0.

“Needless to say, it was a tough decision and one I thought about and discussed at length with my family and team.

“Ultimately, the opportunity to spend more time at home with my family, reduce international travel, focus on senior golf and have the opportunity to pursue other interests was something that I felt was right for me at this stage of my life and career.

“Clearly, LIV Golf has divided opinion, but to be part of the founding group that took world class golf around the globe, showcased our great game to a new audience, built a team brand in Majesticks GC, helped innovate tournament formats and establish a leading community impact program in Little Sticks, is something I will be forever proud of. And that’s just scratching the surface of what we achieved together.

“Change is never easy and it’s fair to say professional golf has experienced plenty of it over the last few years. But I’ve always believed that change can create opportunity and ultimately lead to positive outcomes. There will undoubtedly be more changes ahead, but I am confident the game will continue to grow, evolve, and deliver the very best for golf fans around the world.

“I’m immensely grateful to everyone who has been part of my journey with LIV Golf, from my teammates and colleagues, league staff, partners and of course the fans who supported us along the way – thank you! We’ve shared some incredible experiences, created great memories, and built friendships that will last well beyond the golf course. Whatever happens next, I wish you nothing but the very best for the future.”

As for what’s next, the 50-year-old, who made just shy of $14 million in five years on LIV, added: “I’m genuinely excited about this next chapter. I’m looking forward to spending more time with my family, continuing to develop The Postman YouTube channel, sharing more of my life, golf, experiences and competing in some senior events.

“Something I am also particularly looking forward to is being able to spend more time helping [eldest son] Luke as he pursues his career in professional golf, and [youngest son] Joshua as he looks to develop as a golfer in his teenage years. Having spent so many years traveling the world chasing my own golfing dreams, the opportunity to now spend more time supporting my boys as they chase theirs is something that means a great deal to me

“After all these years, golf has given me so much, and I’m excited about what lies ahead, both on and off the course. Thanks again to everyone who has been part of the journey so far! We certainly aren’t done yet!”

A few hours after Poulter’s revelation, Tyrrell Hatton confirmed he would also be on his way out.

In a much more shorter statement, the Ryder Cup and Legion XIII star – who has won 11 times across the PGA Tour, DP World Tour and LIV Golf and made almost $44 million in three seasons on the league – said he “will not be part of 2.0”, adding: “A big thank you to everyone for their continued support. I am excited for what the next chapter of my career holds.”

He concluded that he is “looking forward to seeing you all in Abu Dhabi”, where he will take part in the DP World Tour Playoffs.

Also confirming their LIV Golf exits are Hatton’s Legion XIII teammate Tom McKibbin, Southern Guards’ Branden Grace, and Ripper’s Lucas Herbert.

As it stands, just five players have publicly stated they are prepared to move on with LIV Golf 2.0, which will be funded by a $300 million injection from BC Partners, with the deadline for commitments set for October 25.

title: Australia come back to beat Scotland again in WXV
article_text:
Scotland failed to hang on to a half-time lead against Australia in Canberra as they slumped to a ninth straight Test defeat.

The visitors finish their WXV Global Series campaign with five losses from five, having lost to Canada and New Zealand before three straight defeats by the Wallaroos.

Dave Butcher's side shipped eight tries in their previous outing in Sydney last week and appeared on course for another bruising scoreline when converted scores from Amelia Whitaker and Maya Stewart put the hosts 14-0 up after 12 minutes.

However, the beleaguered tourists responded through captain Rachel Malcolm's opportunistic try and slowly gained a measure of control.

After Australia centre Cecilia Smith was sin-binned for a high tackle on Scotland full-back Chloe Rollie, Aicha Sutcliffe scored the Scots' second try at the back of a rolling maul and Helen Nelson's conversion made it a two-point game.

Australia finished the half with 13 players as Waiaria Ellis joined Smith in the sin-bin and Scotland went in front soon after.

Katie Buchanan skipped past two would-be tacklers to score Scotland's third try and boost hopes that a long-awaited win might be in the offing.

Australia retook the lead just four minutes into the second half though. After Rollie was yellow carded, Faitala Moleka scored the home side's third try, converted by the unerring boot of Sam Wood.

And things went from bad to worse for Scotland when Piper Duck's converted try made it 28-17 on 52 minutes.

Rhona Lloyd hit back after a brilliant carry from Scotland number eight Evie Gallagher, but a Wood penalty and a converted try from home captain Siokapesi Palu Sekona took the game out of reach.

A flurry of cards late on meant both teams finished without a full XV as Lloyd was sin-binned for denying a try-scoring opportunity and Cecilia Smith was shown her second yellow of the match for a high tackle.

Malcolm dotted down for her second try late on, but it was merely a consolation.

Scotland: Chloe Rollie, Rhona Lloyd, Meryl Smith, Helen Nelson, Katie Buchanan; Hannah Ramsay, Leah Brebner-Holden; Anne Young, Aicha Sutcliffe, Elliann Clarke, Holland Bogan, Sarah Bonar, Rachel Malcolm (capt), Rachel McLachlan, Evie Gallagher.

Replacements: Lana Skeldon, Leah Bartlett, Imogen Spence, Hollie Cunningham, Eva Donaldson, Ceitidh Ainsworth, Nicole Flynn, Lucia Scott.

Australia: Faitala Moleka, Maya Stewart, Georgina Friedrichs, Cecilia Smith, Amelia Whitaker; Waiaria Ellis, Samantha Wood; Allana Sikimeti, Tania Naden, Faliki Pohiva, Kaitlin Leaney, Tiarah Minns, Siokapesi Palu Sekona (capt), Emily Chancellor, Piper Duck.

Replacements: Brittany Merlo, Brianna Hoy, Eva Karpani, Michaela Leonard, Pia Tapsell, Lily Bone, Piper Simons, Ella Ryan.

title: Lxme becomes Title Partner of Indian Women’s League
article_text:
Women-focused financial platform Lxme has partnered with Capri Sports to become the title sponsor of the Indian Women’s League (IWL), ahead of the 2026–27 season. The multi-year agreement marks the first major sponsorship milestone since Capri Sports secured a 15-year commercial development and marketing partnership with the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

The financial terms and exact duration of the sponsorship have not been disclosed.

The partnership brings Lxme’s focus on women’s financial independence into Indian women’s football, with the companies aiming to support the league’s growth and improve visibility and opportunities for women athletes.

Capri Sports entered into a 15-year agreement with the AIFF in September 2026 to oversee commercial development and marketing for both the IWL and the second-tier IWL 2. Its remit includes attracting brands and investment, building audiences, increasing the visibility of clubs and players, and strengthening broadcast and digital engagement.

Lxme’s entry as title sponsor is the first major sponsorship announcement under that arrangement. The companies have not yet outlined specific activations or programmes that will be delivered through the partnership.

Jinisha Sharma, director and promoter of Capri Sports, said: “We’ve always believed that women’s sport is good business. It needs investment, attention, and the same commercial ambition that has helped build successful sporting properties around the world.”

She added that the partnership was about bringing together businesses committed to supporting women’s sport and building the future of Indian women’s football.

For Lxme, the sponsorship extends its work in women’s financial empowerment into sport.

Founder Priti Rathi Gupta said: “We see a similar need in sport, where women athletes continue to deserve greater visibility, investment and opportunity.”

The platform said the partnership was a natural extension of its focus on women’s financial independence, while Capri Sports views the association as part of its wider effort to build a sustainable commercial ecosystem around women’s football.

The upcoming IWL season is scheduled to begin on November 13, 2026, with eight clubs competing in 56 matches across Kolkata, Jamshedpur and Bengaluru. Defending champions East Bengal FC will be joined by Sethu FC, Kickstart FC, Nita Football Academy, Gokulam Kerala FC, Garhwal United FC, HOPS FC and Juba Sangha FC. The season is scheduled to conclude on January 23, 2027.

The title sponsorship adds a new commercial partner as the league enters its next phase under Capri Sports’ long-term agreement with the AIFF.

title: Everitt eases Van der Merwe fears amid Scotland hope for Edinburgh youngsters
article_text:
Sean Everitt allayed fears over Duhan van der Merwe despite the winger lasting just 18 minutes on his first appearance of the season for Edinburgh.

Van der Merwe, battled hip and ankle problems all last season and missed the start of the new campaign with the latter issue.

He made his return on Friday but was forced off mid-way through the first half of the capital club's 31-10 victory over the Lions to maintain their winning start to the new URC season.

The timing of the injury was a blow for the two-times British and Irish Lions tourist with Gregor Townsend due to name his Scotland squad for the Nations Championship matches against New Zealand, Australia and Fiji on Monday.

Everitt was unable to provide much detail when he addressed the media immediately post-match but did confirm it was not a recurrence of Van der Merwe's previous injuries.

“Duhan got a laceration to his hand," said the Edinburgh boss, while stating he had not discussed the issue with the club's medical staff.

One player who did further his chances of a Scotland call-up was scrum-half Hector Patterson, who scored twice and was named Player of the Match.

The 21-year-old has been a stand-out performer since breaking into the Edinburgh squad at the end of last season and was singled out by his coach for praise.

"The guys had to work hard for that. We had to keep knocking on the door and I thought we did a lot of damage in the first half.

"The guys chatted in the half-time about keeping doing what we're doing. The guys stuck to the plan and we had a strategy in place for this game and I thought they did really well in executing it.

“It was really difficult conditions to play in. I thought the guys were brave in moving the ball. We said we wanted to move the ball and move the point of contact and I thought they did that really well. We wanted kicking variation and we got a bit of it as well.

“Well done to Hector, he got man of the match. He kicked very well from the base of the ruck as well as set piece. I'm happy with the result and it's good to get five points against the Lions at home.”

Patterson is one of a crop of Edinburgh youngsters who have put themselves in contention at the start of the new season, taking full advantage of a pre-season injury to Ben Vellacott to cement his place in the side.

"Hector's been really good and has sown growth in every game that he's played," Everitt said.

“He was disappointed in his performance last weekend. He came back really strongly tonight and got man of the match. The other nines are going to have to work hard to displace him. That's what we want in the club.”

But with no shortage of competition for scrum-half spots with Scotland, Everitt has urged Patterson to keep working on his game.

Asked if Patterson was ready, Everitt said: “I'm not sure. Are they looking there? Is he ready for test level? Maybe a few more URC games under the belt. He's just got to keep growing his game, becoming more consistent in what he does. It's not easy to get into a national team.

"He's got to understand that. I'm sure he's opening up a few eyes though with his performances."

Another of the Edinburgh youngsters to impress was Liam McConnell, who was again a thorn in the Lions' side at the lineout.

"He just seems to be everywhere on the field. Winning the scraps, winning the kick-offs. Regaining a kick-off return as well," Everitt said of the flanker, while adding he hopes there are also Scotland calls for Magnus Bradbury and Freddy Douglas.

At the other end of the age scale, 36-year-old Grant Gilchrist made his comeback and got through 50 minutes on his first appearance of the season.

Everitt said: "We want to manage guys in their first game back. He hasn't had the opportunity of playing a friendly. He's had the contact training. It was always our plan to take him off early and give Marshall [Sykes] more time in his 100th jersey.

“It was good. He carried well. We know that he runs our line-out. Our line-out functioned very well as well. I thought he did really well in the time he was on the field.”

title: Sam Prendergast doubtful for Ireland’s Argentina opener
article_text:
Sam Prendergast has emerged as a doubt for Ireland’s Nations Championship opener against Argentina after suffering a wrist injury in Leinster training.

The 23-year-old will miss Saturday’s BKT United Rugby Championship clash with Munster at Aviva Stadium, with Joey Carbery starting at out-half for Leinster for the first time since returning to the province.

Leinster head coach Leo Cullen said Prendergast’s recovery is being assessed on a day-by-day basis ahead of Ireland’s meeting with Argentina at Aviva Stadium on November 6.

“He’ll be tight, I’d say,” Cullen said when asked whether Prendergast would be available. “Whether that’s tight positive or tight negative, I’m not quite sure. I genuinely don’t know.”

Cullen added that managing the pain in Prendergast’s wrist was the main concern and said the player had been keen to face Munster before Leinster decided against selecting him.

Prendergast had emerged as the leading candidate for the Ireland number 10 jersey after consecutive man-of-the-match performances against Cardiff and Clermont Auvergne.

Ireland are already without Munster out-half Jack Crowley, who remains sidelined with an injury and was omitted from Andy Farrell’s Nations Championship squad.

Prendergast’s injury could therefore increase the prospect of Ciarán Frawley being considered at out-half against Argentina.

Ireland begin the northern hemisphere phase of the Nations Championship against the Pumas in Dublin on November 6.

Carbery will make his first Leinster start since returning to the province, while captain Dan Sheehan has been selected at number eight against Munster.

Rónan Kelleher starts at hooker, with Sheehan moving into the back row amid Leinster’s injury problems.

Garry Ringrose is unavailable with a hamstring injury, while Caelan Doris is expected to remain sidelined until the new year. Jack Conan will also miss Ireland’s November programme after suffering a dislocated shoulder against Clermont Auvergne.

title: Lee Westwood makes "blind or fools" remark as LIV Golf return row intensifies
article_text:
Lee Westwood says anyone who believes the PGA Tour isn't a rival to the DP World Tour is either "blind or fools", as the Englishman insists LIV Golf players should be allowed back onto the traditional circuits.

The deadline for LIV members to commit to a 2.0 version of the league is fast approaching.

Players have until 25 October to make that decision, but several notables have already made their mind up given the DP World Tour has drawn a line in the sand and stated that any player who signs up to LIV will not have membership in 2027.

Westwood's former European Ryder Cup teammate, Ian Poulter, 50, was among those to jump ship this week.

He was followed out the door by Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy's former mentee Tom McKibbin.

McKibbin insisted he had no regrets over his move, despite previously being advised against the switch by the reigning Masters champion.

Charles Howell III, Abraham Ancer, Branden Grace, David Puig, Lucas Herbert, Thomas Pieters and Adrian Meronk have previously confirmed that they are moving on.

Bryson DeChambeau is yet to make up his mind, but it appears that the two-time U.S. Open champion remains hopeful he can push LIV forward.

Several golfers will return to the DP World Tour in 2027.

Some will be able to play a full schedule given their existing criteria, while it has been rumoured that the European-based circuit may create a separate category for LIV players altogether.

An argument is brewing, with some DPWT golfers expressing disgust that players from the renegade tour may be able to walk back through the door without a hitch.

Dutch veteran Joost Luiten took aim at LIV players before the DP World India Championship, telling Today's Golfer: "There should be a rule that if you gave up your membership you lose all your exemption rights as well.

"Then you have to stay a member if you want to ever come back to this tour.

"A lot of the guys gave up their membership and now they come back like nothing happened and then they become a member again and they get all the rights that they had before they left.

"If they think that they are that good then show it at Q School and beat the guys.

"That's how every other guy that wants to play on this tour has to go."

As far as the 53-year-old is concerned, the DP World Tour is in an "interesting position".

He added: "Caught between needing 'names' at those times of year when they don't get strong fields (Jan-June) [and] giving invites to people who have shown no interest in the tour other than now when they've nowhere else to play.

"And keeping the members happy that support the tour at the smaller events and the lads that have gone through all the qualifying stages.

"Anyone with an exemption should be free to come back because as we know the DPWT endorses members going to another rival tour and already have 10 cards for it but if people don't have an exemption they should have to go through the school like everyone else.

"And anyone that thinks the PGA Tour aren't rivals and are partners are either blind or fools.

"Yes they provide funding now but to what end and at what cost to the DPWT? The end of 2027 will be interesting as to what assets they ask for."

Westwood was referring to the DP World Tour's strategic alliance with the PGA Tour.

Officials from both sides have stated an extension to the deal is currently being negotiated.

A deep dive from the Money In Sport newsletter recently painted a grim picture for the DP World Tour.

In 2025 alone, the DP World Tour recorded an operating loss of nearly £65m. The PGA Tour invested £58m.

title: Lee Westwood responds to suggestions some LIV players should not be allowed back on the DP World Tour
article_text:
LIV golfers are jumping ship left, right, and center, and flocking to the DP World Tour.

The floodgates have opened: Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton, Lucas Herbert, and Tom McKibbin all announced their departure from the rebel golf league on the same day, returning to their roots next season.

They'll join Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia, and Joaquin Niemann in what is set to be an immensely strong DP World Tour in 2027. This is exciting news for the tour, which will have many more eyes on it next season, but it's not that popular among players.

A few DP World Tour players have complained that LIV golfers are returning to the tour unpunished and taking spots from those who stayed loyal. Two DP World Tour winners have named players they don't want to see return next season, and Lee Westwood responded.

As LIV players seek a return to the DP World Tour next season, tour members are voicing concerns about which golfers will be allowed back.

Three-time DP World Tour winner Ewen Ferguson said he doesn't want to see those who criticised the tour while on LIV return now that they are out of options.

He posted to X, "I have to say, some of the LIV players coming back to play DP is actually cool as some really good players, but hilarious how some of them slammed the tour for so long, not one good thing to say about it, now it's the best thing since sliced bread and feels like coming home 🤔."

Another DP World Tour winner, Richard Mansell, agreed, replying to Ferguson's post: "Spot on my mate. I haven't been around the tour a lot this year and when I have since coming back from injury my golf hasn't been where I want it so I don't want to say too much. However, things are going to look different in 2027. Some should be allowed back and some shouldn't…"

A number of LIV players have been openly critical of the DP World Tour for various reasons. Rahm spent much of 2026 battling the DP World Tour for his membership and publicly accused the tour of "extorting" players.

Meanwhile, Poulter and Westwood were furious about the tour's sanctions for players who joined LIV Golf.

Ferguson and Mansell were likely talking about Westwood and Poulter in their X posts, but Westwood still shared his take on the matter.

Westwood, who often shares his thoughts on LIV Golf and the DP World Tour on X, responded to Ferguson's post.

The 25-time winner on the DP World Tour said, "It's an interesting position the @DPWorldTour finds itself in. Caught between needing 'names' at those times of year when they don't get strong fields (Jan-June).

"Giving invites to people who have shown no interest in the tour other than now when they've nowhere else to play. And keeping the members happy that support the tour at the smaller events and the lads that have gone through all the qualifying stages.

"Anyone with an exemption should be free to come back because as we know the DPWT endorses members going to another rival tour and already have 10 cards for it but if people don't have an exemption they should have to go through the school like everyone else.

"And anyone that thinks the PGA tour aren't rivals and are partners are either blind or fools. Yes they provide funding now but to what end and at what cost to the DPWT? The end of 2027 will be interesting as to what assets they ask for."

It's a confusing post that doesn't address Ferguson's point. Westwood is among those who have criticised the tour in recent years, and he didn't explain why he thinks he and Poulter should be allowed back if they wish.

Westwood is right that the DP World Tour faces a conundrum, and it will be interesting to see how they navigate this over the coming months.

title: LIV Golf 2.0: Who’s in and who’s out ahead of deadline day?
article_text:
Which players are leaving LIV Golf? And who is sticking around for the league’s 2.0 era? This is everything you need to know…

The deadline for LIV Golf players to decide whether they will stick or twist is almost here.

The league has until October 25 to convince key names to sign up for the new iteration of the league ahead of a possible $300 million investment from credit firm BC Partners.

And it is crucial that the league persuades some big hitters to stay for its relaunch. But the DP World Tour’s move to reject memberships for players who hope to sign up to LIV 2.0 has made LIV’s prospects a whole lot more difficult.

So far, these are the players who have said they will be sticking around should LIV 2.0 come to fruition…

Englishman Bland was the first player to commit to LIV 2.0. The Cleeks star told Tom Hobbs of Flushing It: “Apart from the Legends Tour, I have nowhere else to play. I’m banned until next August on the PGA Tour Champions, and I don’t have the desire to go back to the DP World Tour and start from the bottom again. I’m too old for that. I’m 54 next year and I’m done chasing after the game and trying to work my way up the ladder. I’ve done that for 25 years. The last few years on LIV have been absolutely brilliant and if LIV doesn’t come off, I’ll play the senior majors.”

Another player who has told Flushing It he will stay is Tringale. The 39-year-old American, whose only victory in nearly 20 years as a pro was the 2014 Franklin Templeton Shootout, has earned north of $18 million in his five years on the league.

Tringale’s HyFlyers teammate said in August: “I’m committed to being here. This is where I want to be. This has been home to me for the last four years, it’s been great. I’m happy to stay.”

“As of today, I play for the Cleeks,” the Frenchman told Golf Planete in September. “I hope the situation gets resolved, and I hope there’s a future for LIV 2.0 because they have been some really great tournaments. There are people there who genuinely gave me my smile back and helped me rediscover the enjoyment I had maybe lost a little during my second year in the United States.” Perez added: “Playing fewer tournaments gave me a lot more mental clarity and allowed me to really appreciate the opportunity we have – to be here, to travel the world and play golf. I think that if LIV hadn’t existed, I might not have found that again. So naturally, I hope it continues.”

The New Zealander, who played on Bubba Watson’s RangeGoats team last year, has told TG he definitely wants to return to LIV next year as he recovers from hip surgery.

The two-time major champion has had one foot out the door for months, but his exit was confirmed via a bankruptcy hearing in New Jersey. Rahm’s lawyer said he deemed the conditions for a LIV 2.0 contract “unacceptable.” Three individual titles and over $100 million in prize money alone, Rahm’s years on LIV were nothing if not lucrative.

Rahm’s Legion XIII and Ryder Cup sidekick also released a short statement saying he “will not be part of LIV 2.0”.

And McKibbin makes it three. The Northern Irishman posted on social media: “After two seasons with Legion XIII, I have decided not to sign with LIV Golf for its next chapter. I will be playing a full schedule on the DP World Tour in 2027. Joining LIV Golf was the right decision for me at the time, and I’m grateful for everything it has given me. Playing alongside Jon, Tyrrell and Caleb [Surratt] taught me more than I could have imagined. Thank you to them, the team staff and everyone at LIV Golf for making me feel at home from day one. I’ve taken time to think about what’s best for me and I am confident this to is the right decision to help me achieve my goals. Thank you to everyone who has supported me over the last two years. See you in 2027.”

The Englishman, now 50, has decided he will not move forward with LIV Golf, instead deciding to concentrate on spending more time with his family – particularly his sons, Luke and Joshua, who are budding golfers themselves.

The 2010 Open champion and Southern Guards captain was speaking at the Link Hong Kong Open when he declared himself out. “It’s time to move on,” Oosthuizen said. “It’s a lot of international travel for single events.”

Joining his Southern Guards skipper is the nine-time DP World Tour winner, who told South African broadcaster SuperSport that returning “feels like coming home. He added: “Some of the proudest moments of my career have happened on this Tour, from my four-time win breakthrough season in 2012 to winning the Investec South African Open in front of home fans. I am hungrier than ever to compete and write the next chapter of my career on the global stage. My time on the LIV Tour was a memorable chapter, especially getting to travel the world and compete alongside some of my closest friends in the game.”

“I don’t see myself playing in the LIV 2.0,” Puig said at the Open de Espana. “It’s a decision I’ve made. I hope to play the European Tour next year, which I really enjoy, with a fuller schedule.”

title: 'Joining LIV Golf was the right decision for me at the time'

title: Yuto Katsuragawa equals course record to move ahead in Korea
article_text:
Yuto Katsuragawa tied the course record with a flawless 63 to surge into a two-shot lead at the 2026 Genesis Championship.

The Japanese was fighting to keep his playing privileges for the 2027 DP World Tour when beginning the week in 106th place on the Race to Dubai Rankings delivered by DP World.

With only the top 100 guaranteed to retain their card for next season, Katsuragawa knew he needed a good week but even he would have surprised himself with his stunning third round at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club.

He started five shots behind overnight leaders Casey Jarvis and Antoine Rozner, with the former bursting three shots clear during his front nine.

However, Katsuragawa enjoyed a birdie blitz on his outward nine before birdieing three of the last five holes to match the eight-under round of Jinam Kang in 2006.

"It's been a long time since I had this good feeling so it was a great round," Katsuragawa said.

"After the Irish Open, I met a new putting coach and he was very helpful to get me in good form like this today.

"I've been outside of the 100 (on the Race to Dubai Rankings delivered by DP World), but I've been aiming up and now I can look up to victory, and go all the way to play my golf."

Jarvis made an early move with a birdie at the second to reach 11 under, with Katsuragawa rolling in four straight birdies from the same hole to sit two behind.

A birdie at the fifth saw Jarvis increase his lead to three, and although Katsuragawa matched him at the eighth, the South African carded another at the next to climb to 13 under.

The leader dropped his first shot at the seventh, but immediately birdied the next to restore his three-shot advantage.

Si Woo Kim then joined Katsuragawa on double figures after his fourth birdie of the day at the 12th.

Katsuragawa got back on the birdie trail at the 14th and 15th to close in on Jarvis, who had just hit his tee-shot at the 12th out of bounds to stall his round.

He salvaged a bogey as he dropped back to 12 under alongside Katsuragawa, only to drop a shot at the next to hand the Japanese the outright lead.

A brilliant approach into the last set up a birdie putt of three feet for Katsuragawa, who drained the effort with confidence to set the clubhouse mark of 13 under par.

Jarvis could only par his way home, despite hitting the cup with his chipped third shot at the par-five last, as he became Katsuragawa's closest rival at 11 under.

Rozner battled back from bogeys at the second and third with birdies at the 15th and 18th to join South Korean pair Sanghun Shin and Kim at ten under.

Spaniard Jorge Campillo, France's Martin Couvra and Open Champion Ryan Fox were one shot further back, while Frenchman Frederic Lacroix, England's Dan Bradbury, Japan's Rikuya Hoshino and American Johannes Veerman were at eight under.

title: No panic for England but Mitchell issues PWR warning
article_text:
Before England's three-match series against Canada, few would have predicted this outcome.

A 2-0 series defeat for the Red Roses; their record 39-match winning streak and 41-match unbeaten run – stretching back nearly four years – ended; and consecutive losses for the first time since 2016.

Over the past 13 months, Canada have turned a 33-13 defeat in the World Cup final into a statement 31-22 win in Ottawa. And three years out from the 2029 World Cup, they have laid down an early marker of their title credentials.

More than that, they have proved England are not invincible – a reality which should hearten New Zealand and perennial Women's Six Nations bridesmaids France because both have beaten giant-killers Canada in the past 12 months.

For the second time in eight days, England captain Meg Jones has been called upon to take stock of a defeat. Once again, she opted for a message of defiance.

"It was a hell of a contest. We're not broken, we just need to grow," said Jones. "Do it together, use the lessons. We're playing the best teams, getting the best punches thrown at us.

"I genuinely believe we've got the best players in the world. When we're firing, generally we're unstoppable. We don't dwell on the past, we're not anxious about the future, we're focused on the present."

It's true, this is far from panic stations. In 2016, England were the defending world champions when they lost to France and beaten finalists Canada. Since then, they've been imperious, winning a second World Cup, reaching the final in 2017 and 2022, and lifting nine of the past 10 Six Nations titles.

This is only their third defeat in 74 matches, so perspective is required.

But England's performances throughout the WXV Global Series highlighted areas for improvement.

They have lacked their usual clinical edge in attack. In Ottawa, Sarah Bern was held up over the line and England conceded a turnover less than five metres out as they failed to make their dominance pay before the break.

Tellingly, they opted to kick a penalty early in the second half to close the deficit – perhaps a lesson learned from last month's 26-26 draw in Exeter, where they turned down a shot at goal to snatch the win in the dying moments.

In defence, they have conceded 18 tries across their past five matches in the WXV, compared to eight in six at the World Cup. They have trailed at the break three times, something they hadn't experienced since 2020.

Last week, ill-discipline repeatedly gifted Canada field position before a late handling error, which put a clearing kick under pressure, opened the door for the hosts' winning try.

On Friday night, Gabrielle Senft picked off a bouncing ball from a missed pass to set up Canada's second try. Minutes later, England were lucky not to concede a similar try when a pass bisected Jess Breach and Jones, who pounced on the ball just before Lizzie Gibson got to it.

"We were riding the waves, building phases, scrum, set piece, we were very strong. Sometimes it's the bounce of the ball or it doesn't swing your way. We couldn't execute when we got in their 22, that's a big one to reflect on for sure," said Jones.

Canada does not have a professional women's domestic league and their players had to launch a crowd-funding campaign before the last World Cup to cover the cost of their training camps.

It's unsurprising, therefore, that many of Canada's top talents play domestically in England's Premiership Women's Rugby, which offers a level of training and match experience they cannot find elsewhere.

Twenty-five Canadian players are contracted for the 2026-27 season, with 11 featuring in July's PWR final between Saracens and Trailfinders. Three Canadian coaches, including head coach Kevin Rouet at Saracens, are also involved in English domestic rugby.

PWR squads must have a minimum of 13 England qualified players in a matchday squad.

But England head coach John Mitchell has warned that too many overseas players in the PWR could be detrimental for future Red Roses sides.

"I think it's necessary to make sure that young English girls are getting enough PWR time," Mitchell said. "It's a critical pathway because Sevens is definitely gone. For players aged between 19 and 23, it's critical.

"We're just going to make sure we don't erode our depth as a result of [overseas involvement]. It's not so much about now. It will be the future that will suffer if we're not smart in that area."

Mitchell has been forced to call upon England's squad depth on multiple occasions in 2026 with Abby Dow and Emily Scarratt retiring after the World Cup, four players absent through pregnancy, and several big names – including Hannah Botterman, Alex Matthews, and Amy Cokayne – spending time on the sidelines because of injury.

He's handed out more than half a dozen debuts this year, with hooker Bryony Field particularly impressing during September's home internationals, played the likes of Abi Burton and Ellie Kildunne out of position, and brought Liz Crake back into the fold after several years away.

title: Bath issue ominous double injury update: 'I’d be amazed if it wasn’t bad news'
article_text:
Gloucester head coach George Skivington hailed his side’s resilience and character after seeing them triumph 23-5 over Bath in a pulsating encounter to remain top of the Gallagher Prem table.

A win was a remarkable achievement in the circumstances as they overcame a first-half battering from their opponents, who were held up over the line on at least three occasions.

Furthermore Gloucester conceded 22 penalties and received yellow cards for Ollie Thorley, Ciaran Knight and Will Joseph but still finished the stronger to record their first win over Bath at Kingsholm since 2022.

Freddie Thomas and Max Llewellyn scored Gloucester’s tries with George Barton converting both and adding three penalties, whereas a try from Kepueli Tuipulotu was Bath’s sole response.

Skivington said: “Everything that could go against us tonight did as we were pinged off the park and went down to 13 men so we were just hanging in there.

“Bath had opportunity after opportunity to score but despite having everything thrown at us, they never let it faze them and we never looked like throwing the towel in.

“Bath at home is the number one fixture for our fans and we want to make Kingsholm a fortress and make sure everyone who bought a ticket wants to buy another one.

“Ultimately we want to play attacking rugby and the lads stayed brave tonight. It may not have been the right decision at the end but Will Joseph rolled the dice to create Max Llewellyn’s try.

“However it wasn’t our best performance as we weren’t accurate enough but the resilience and character of the squad got us over the line.”

For Bath it was a third defeat on the bounce having been beaten convincingly by Northampton and Montpellier in their previous fixtures, so 126 points have been conceded during that time.

However they will wonder how they failed to score in the first half as their pack secured enough possession to have won three games.

To complete their miserable night they lost internationals, Santi Carreras and Guy Pepper to injuries.

Bath’s Director of Rugby, Johann van Graan, said: “Both Santi and Guy will have scans so it’s too early to assess but in Santi’s case I’d be amazed if it wasn’t bad news.

“I’m frustrated as we created so many opportunities but didn’t finish them and if you don’t finish them you can’t build pressure.

“The big moment of the game came early in the second half when we were only 9-5 down and had a try disallowed.

“Our plans to get over the line are working but we’ll have to work harder at how we get the ball to the floor.

“I’m still pretty calm as parts of our game are really going well but we need to score tries to build pressure.”

title: Impressive Gloucester beat Bath to extend lead at top of Prem
article_text:
Gloucester stormed to their first win over Bath in the Prem at Kingsholm since April 2022 with a 23-5 victory built on an immense defensive display.

The Cherry and Whites were down to 13 men for a period of the first half but led 9-5 at half-time, having repelled wave after wave of Bath pressure on their tryline.

George Barton then kicked three successive penalties to put the hosts 9-0 up before Kepu Tuipulotu pulled a try back just before the break from a driving maul.

Freddie Thomas scored under the posts to stretch Gloucester's lead further midway through the second half and Max Llewellyn had Kingsholm raucous when he rolled over with two minutes to go for a famous victory that reaffirms their status as league leaders.

This was Gloucester's first victory over their oldest rivals since their 64-0 thrashing of Bath more than four and a half years earlier, months before Johann van Graan took over at The Rec and transformed the Bath team.

After an impressive draw against holders Bordeaux in the Champions Cup seven days earlier, George Skivington said this was the Cherry and Whites' biggest game of the season and their performance showed it is no fluke that they lead the Prem at this early stage of the campaign, even with captain Dewi Lake and centre Seb Atkinson absent through injury.

For Bath, it is a third defeat in a row in all competitions, their lowest amount of Prem points scored under Van Graan, and all compounded by the losses of full-back Santiago Carreras to a possible anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury, while flanker Guy Pepper also went off injured.

For a chunk of the first half, Gloucester were all but penned by their own tryline, with Bath enjoying 97% possession at one point for 10 minutes, but they could not find a way through.

Tuipulotu was held up over the line and the TMO three times intervened to scratch off Bath tries; once as Tuipulotu made a double movement, the second when Prem debutant Tyler Offiah hit touch before passing to Louie Hennessey and again when Enoch Opoku-Gyamfi dropped the ball over the line.

The penalties were simultaneously mounting against Gloucester, with Ollie Thorley and Ciaran Knight both sent to the sin-bin for repeated infringements - but they stood up to the fight, making 113 first-half tackles while their fans cheered any turnover as if they had scored.

When Gloucester did seize possession, they kicked downfield and won successive penalties of their own, with Barton coolly stepping up to the tee to slot all three over.

Tuipulotu finally got his try late in the first half but it would be the only points Bath would score all night.

The Bath hooker was held up on the line again early in the second half and even when Gloucester had Will Joseph yellow-carded for a deliberate knock-on, Bath could not capitalise, with the hosts again the ones to score.

They kicked to the corner with their first bit of possession in Bath's 22 during the half and after the maul drove forward, Thomas barged through and stretched over.

Llewellyn then added the finishing touches in the closing stages, while a Finn Russell mis-kick to touch summed up Bath's night.

"Everything that could have got thrown against the boys did, we were getting pinged off the park and it felt like the boys couldn't quite win the referee over - that happens in games sometimes.

"I thought the boys' character and the attritional nature of that game, and the fact that no one took a backwards step or threw the towel in, was unbelievable.

"The defensive performance and the connectivity against the odds was testament to the boys."

"You can't build pressure if you don't finish your opportunities. We got in there loads of times. The big moment is just after half-time, the score's 9-5, we get the post penalty and the try is not allowed, so frustration.

"The fact that we are over the tryline means the plan to get there is working, we've got to work harder as a group to make sure we actually get the ball on the floor."

On Carreras' injury: "He's got to go for a scan, I'd be amazed if that's not really bad news, which is gutting for him."

Gloucester: Barton; Thorley, Joseph, Llewellyn, W Knight; C Atkinson, Englefield; Rapava Ruskin, Blake, C Knight, Kleyn, Clark, Thomas, Morgan (capt), Clement.

Replacements: Innard, Bleuler, Fasogbon, Trenholm, Ludlow, Robson, M Knight, Redshaw.

Sin-bin: Thorley (21), C Knight (28), Joseph (46).

Bath: Carreras; Hennessey, Lawrence, Redpath, Offiah; Russell, Spencer (capt); Obano, Tuipulotu, Griffin, Opoku-Gyamfi, Ewels, Bayliss, Pepper, Reid.

Replacements: Frost, Kirk, Verden, Molony, Hill, Carr-Smith, Donoghue, Green.

title: ‘I gave everything’ – The 4 Grand Slam winners retiring in 2026 as 17 stars bow out

Some names will leave an indelible mark on tennis for years, if not decades, to come. Others will slip quietly away into the annals of history, but still have a lot to be proud of.

For some, tennis fans will argue certain individuals left without going out in a way they deserve, and others had retirement forced upon them by injury.

Some players won majors, others reached the top 10, and a handful cracked the top 100 as well. Without further ado, here are the 17 players whose careers on the ATP Tour came to a halt in 2026.

The 41-year-old is bringing down the curtain on a remarkable career after 24 years on the circuit. Wawrinka‘s last official tournament is set to be in his native Switzerland next week at the Basel Open, although he will play an exhibition in December, too.

The Canadian reached a career-high of No 3 in 2016, the year he reached the Wimbledon final, where the big server beat Federer in the semi-finals, only to lose to Andy Murray in the showpiece event.

The 6ft 5in player, who turned pro in 2008, had a number of injury issues but ended up winning eight singles titles and was a repeat ATP Finals qualifier. The 35-year-old made it to four Masters 1000 finals before hanging up his racket in January, 18 months after his final match.

The flamboyant Frenchman has been a fan favourite for years. His athleticism, shot-making and showmanship have endeared him to fans across the planet but now, the 40-year-old’s time as a professional is over.

The former world No 6 was supposed to play in Lyon in Paris before retiring but the sudden end of his marriage with Elina Svitolina put pay to that. Monfils won 13 singles titles in a 22-year career.

title: Study: For brands, Fever broadcasts and social media among the most valuable in sports
article_text:
During the 2026 WNBA regular season, the Indiana Fever generated $40.3M in value for its brand partners via social media posts, according to data from Trajektory, the most of any of the league’s 15 clubs and more than all but four teams across MLB, NBA, NHL, NFL, MLS and NWSL.

The ranking is based on nearly 51,000 team posts made from May 8 through Sept. 24, across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and X tracked by the Chicago-based sports sponsorship intelligence and analytics platform.

Inter Miami CF provided a study-leading $102.2M in social value to its sponsors, bolstered by $24M via its Royal Caribbean partnership.

On TV broadcasts, Fever sponsors gained more than 232 hours of on-screen exposure, which generated a league-high $464.3M in media and sponsorship value.

Gainbridge’s arena naming rights of the Fever’s home and Eli Lilly’s jersey patch sponsorship of the team demonstrated how strategic asset placement drives massive returns. In addition to $27.7M in TV exposure, Gainbridge secured $1.1M in social value and expanded that with $2.8M in “earned TV partner value” from external sources, such as news coverage and highlight shows.

Similarly, Lilly’s jersey patch generated $4.4M from social and $1.4M in value across earned TV.

title: Top rugby match halted for serious incident as player consoled by team-mate
article_text:
The WXV Global Series fixture between Japan and Wales was brought to a halt during the second half following a serious injury sustained by Freya Bell. Proceedings were suspended for over six minutes, with medical personnel from both sides treating the Wales player on the field at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium in Tokyo. At 52 minutes and with Wales ahead 7-0, centre Bell collapsed clutching her leg following a clear-out at a ruck.

Play initially carried on around her as she remained on the ground gripping her leg in visible distress, with a Wales medic attending to her. The referee subsequently called a stoppage, allowing Bell to receive treatment.

"Freya Bell looks in some real discomfort there," BBC Wales commentator Gareth Rees Owen said.

"Her right knee I think? Oh no. Just a horrible sight.

He added: "Our concerns are now with Freya Bell. Oh goodness."

Co-commentator and former Wales international Philippa Tuttiett added: "They do seem to be isolating that knee. Such a young player as well."

Wales co-captain Alex Callender, marking her 50th cap, was seen consoling her team-mate as the medical staff attempted to help Bell, who was in agony on the floor.

"Absolutely not (good to see)," Tuttiett noted as three medical professionals worked on Bell's leg, who were subsequently assisted by the Japanese support team. "Especially for the players left on the field, seeing your team-mate go down like that."

Following a lengthy delay, Bell was carried off the pitch on a stretcher, which will undoubtedly be a major worry for Wales head coach Sean Lynn.

Owen continued: "It's so nice to see Alex Callender there supporting her."

Bell was substituted by Courtney Keight.

Wales took the lead courtesy of Seren Lockwood's opening try, which Bell successfully converted in the first half.
